roastText: Congrats, you’ve turned a basic pedometer into a digital goldfish bowl. The tech is trivial, the market is saturated, and your users will tire of pixelated guppies faster than they burn calories. Unless you’ve got a secret partnership with a fish retailer, this is just another vanity metric chase.
feasNote: Tech is a walk in the park
origNote: Seen it, done it, ignored it

advice.text: Add a real‑world reward tied to health outcomes.
Slash development costs and launch as a simple widget.
If you must fish, make them NFT‑exclusive.

idea: I want to build a mobile app that turns users’ daily step counts into points they can spend on virtual fish, aquarium backgrounds, and decorative accessories.

roastText: Surprisingly you’ve identified a real pain point instead of reinventing the toothbrush. Your integration claim sounds feasible, but expect endless API wrangling and a support nightmare. Pricing a flat subscription might work, yet you’ll need to convince dentists that texting isn’t a gimmick. If you pull this off, you might actually make something dentists don’t immediately ignore.

advice.text: Focus on one dominant scheduling platform first
Build rock‑solid customer support from day one
Add analytics to justify the subscription cost

idea: I want to build a tool for small dental clinics that automatically detects cancelled appointments, texts waitlisted patients, and fills open slots. It integrates with their existing scheduling software and charges each clinic a monthly subscription.

roastText: You think people will pay for virtual ownership of something they can experience for free in their backyard. Your 'innovation' is a masterclass in rebranding the mundane as unique, but it's still a house of cards. The environmental impact of NFTs is already a concern, and now you want to tokenise a leaf? Please, tell me more about how you plan to revolutionise the world with digitised detritus. Your concept is an insult to the very notion of scarcity and value.

advice.text: Consider an educational platform about nature instead
Abandon this NFT idea before you lose everything
Research the environmental impact of your 'innovation' before proceeding

idea: I want to create a website where users can turn nature into NFT such as air, leaves, rocks, etc.
